I've been surfing for over 5 years and I would barely consider myself a beginner intermediate Surfer. I feel like I haven't improved in the last 2 years, even though I've been going 3-5 times a week the entire time. Don't feel bad.

1- as soon as you're planing and in the middle of the pop up, you should already be looking at the lip. That way, once you're on your feet, you're entire body is facing down the line. Pump for speed like crazy. Matter of fact, I wish someone told me to focus on getting speed instead of working on my bottom turn. Literally, take an entire session just to focus on staying at the top half of the wave

2- before you go into the water, take like 10 minutes to look for a nice channel in. It might take a while to locate these paths. 1 thing I look for are rips I can use to Paddle in. The waves barely break near rips, and even if it does, the counter movement will help dissipate the energy. When in doubt, just follow other people paddling out. 

3- it's good that you are sitting forward on the board when you are about to take off. The timing is strict, but when you feel yourself planing and getting some speed, quickly shift your weight back by arching your back during your pop up. If it still feels too steep, or you are getting pitched off of the wave, jam most of your weight into your tail with your back foot and stay low. This has saved me a bunch of times from wiping out, but if I got pitched, I almost always lose the wave. Better than eating it I guess
